ui_ux_improvements.title: Add Keyboard Controls Support
ui_ux_improvements.description: Implement keyboard input as an alternative to mouse-only controls, allowing players to use arrow keys or WASD for movement and spacebar for firing.
ui_ux_improvements.rationale: The game currently only supports mouse input (input.js handles mousemove/mousedown only). Keyboard controls provide a more familiar gaming experience for many players and are essential for accessibility. Users without precise mouse control or those preferring traditional arcade-style controls are currently excluded.
ui_ux_improvements.current_state: Input.js only registers mousemove, mousedown, and mouseup events. No keyboard event listeners exist anywhere in the codebase. Player movement is controlled exclusively by mouse X position.
ui_ux_improvements.proposed_change: Add keydown/keyup event listeners in input.js to track arrow keys or WASD. Add a leftPressed/rightPressed state. Modify player.js updatePlayer() to accept keyboard input in addition to mouse. Add spacebar as alternative fire trigger. Update instructions in index.html to show keyboard controls.
ui_ux_improvements.user_benefit: Players can choose their preferred control scheme. Those with motor control difficulties or those on laptops without precision mice can play effectively. Provides a more traditional arcade game feel.

ui_ux_improvements.title: Add Audio Mute/Volume Control
ui_ux_improvements.description: Add a UI control to mute or adjust the volume of game audio effects. Currently the game has an extensive procedural audio system but no way for users to control volume.
ui_ux_improvements.rationale: The audio.js module generates procedural sounds for explosions, firing, level transitions, etc. There's no mute button or volume slider despite audio being a significant part of the experience. Users in shared spaces, those with audio sensitivity, or those who simply prefer silent play have no control option. The glow slider in settings shows UI patterns exist but audio controls are missing.
ui_ux_improvements.current_state: Audio system in audio.js creates sounds directly to audioContext.destination. No master gain node exists for volume control. The settings div only contains a glow intensity slider. No audio control UI exists in the HTML.
ui_ux_improvements.proposed_change: Add a master GainNode in audio.js between all audio and the destination. Create a mute toggle button and/or volume slider in the settings section of index.html alongside the glow slider. Add localStorage persistence for audio settings similar to glow intensity. Style the control to match the existing cyan/retro aesthetic.
ui_ux_improvements.user_benefit: Users can play in quiet environments, adjust audio to comfortable levels, or completely mute sounds while preserving visual effects. Respects user preference and environment.

ui_ux_improvements.title: Add Pause Functionality with ESC Key
ui_ux_improvements.description: Implement a pause system that allows players to pause and resume gameplay using the ESC key, with a visible pause overlay showing game controls and resume option.
ui_ux_improvements.rationale: The game runs continuously once started with no way to pause. Players cannot take breaks, answer interruptions, or check controls mid-game. The gameActive flag in game.js tracks game state but there's no pause mechanism. This is a fundamental gameplay feature expected in any modern game.
ui_ux_improvements.current_state: game.js has a gameActive boolean but no gamePaused state. The update loop runs unconditionally. No keydown handler for ESC exists. No pause overlay exists in the HTML.
ui_ux_improvements.proposed_change: Add a gamePaused state in game.js. Add ESC keydown listener in input.js that toggles pause. Create a pause overlay in index.html styled similarly to gameOver div (semi-transparent background, cyan text). Show 'PAUSED' message with 'Press ESC to Resume' and list game controls. Modify update() to skip game logic when paused but continue rendering for visual freeze effect.
ui_ux_improvements.user_benefit: Players can pause to handle interruptions, study the game state, or take breaks without losing progress. Essential for longer play sessions and accessibility.

ui_ux_improvements.title: Add Screen Shake on Player Damage
ui_ux_improvements.description: Implement a camera shake effect when the player takes damage (loses a life) to provide stronger visual feedback of the impact.
ui_ux_improvements.rationale: When the player is hit by alien missiles (missiles.js line ~860), only an explosion particle and sound play. There's no camera feedback. The flashScreen() function exists in particles.js for shrapnel hits but isn't consistently used. Screen shake is a game design best practice for conveying impact and creates visceral feedback.
ui_ux_improvements.current_state: When decreaseLives() is called in game.js, only the UI updates. missiles.js creates an explosion and plays a sound on player hit. No camera perturbation occurs. The camera in main.js has smooth interpolation but no shake system.
ui_ux_improvements.proposed_change: Add a cameraShake() function in game.js or main.js that adds temporary random offsets to camera position. Call this on player damage. Use dampened oscillation (e.g., offset = amplitude * sin(time * frequency) * exp(-decay * time)). The effect should last ~300ms with decreasing intensity. Optionally add a red screen vignette flash for extra impact.
ui_ux_improvements.user_benefit: Players immediately understand they've been hit through visceral visual feedback. Increases game feel and engagement. Makes damage more noticeable during intense gameplay.

ui_ux_improvements.title: Add Collapsible Settings Menu with Gear Icon
ui_ux_improvements.description: Replace the always-visible settings section at the bottom of the screen with a gear icon that expands to show settings, reducing screen clutter during gameplay.
ui_ux_improvements.rationale: The current settings div with the glow slider is always visible at the bottom of the screen, taking up space and adding visual noise during gameplay. Modern games typically hide settings behind an icon. This would also make room for additional settings (audio controls, potentially more options) without cluttering the main view.
ui_ux_improvements.current_state: The #settings div is positioned absolute at bottom center, always visible with the label 'GLOW INTENSITY' and a slider. It competes visually with the instructions text above it. No toggle/collapse mechanism exists.
ui_ux_improvements.proposed_change: Add a gear icon (using CSS or unicode glyph) in the corner (e.g., bottom-right near version). Clicking the gear opens a settings panel with current glow slider plus future audio controls. Panel slides in/out or fades. Add CSS for panel styling matching retro aesthetic. Move instructions to be toggleable too or shown only on first visit.
ui_ux_improvements.user_benefit: Cleaner gameplay view with less distraction. Settings accessible when needed but not constantly visible. Creates room for adding more settings without cluttering the screen.

metadata.notes: Analysis performed through static code review. Visual verification recommended via browser testing. Key findings: no keyboard controls, no audio volume control, no pause functionality, limited damage feedback, settings always visible.
additional_considerations: Touch/mobile support - game has no touch event handlers for mobile devices
Color blind mode - relies heavily on red/green for damage/health states
Loading indicator - no visual feedback during initial THREE.js scene setup
Power-up feedback - limited visual feedback when collecting power-ups
Boss health bar entrance animation - appears abruptly without intro animation
